coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 8–10 miles, Z2 only (130–140 bpm), no vert work. Your resting HR is 19 bpm above your 30-day average at 83 bpm, and recovery score is 55/100—both signals of incomplete parasympathetic recovery. You're 50 days from the Alps and in taper; this is the phase where you *preserve* fitness, not chase it. The long run Saturday will carry the stimulus; today is about clearing fatigue and letting your nervous system settle. Keep it flat, conversational, sub-150 bpm average.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Eat to your elevated resting HR and sleep debt. You logged 9.34 hours of sleep last night, which is good volume, but elevated RHR suggests systemic stress—likely travel, travel meals, or accumulated glycogen deficit. Consume 60–80g carbs with breakfast and lunch today (oats, rice, pasta), and hit 25–30g protein at each meal to support recovery. Hydrate aggressively: your body needs it to drop that RHR. Skip any calorie restriction or 'fasted runs' this week.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep is your primary tool right now, not ice baths or massages. Aim for 9 hours again tonight—your system is signaling it needs it. The elevated resting HR and moderate recovery score suggest sympathetic dominance; sleep is the only reliable reset. If you're traveling today for work, prioritize a dark, cool hotel room and skip the late client dinner if possible. A 20-minute nap (1400–1420) can help bridge the gap if night sleep is compromised.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: Resist the taper demons. You're 50 days out with 48.2 miles last week—solid volume—and now you're cutting. It feels slow and weak. It's not. The Julian Alps 50K demands peak glycogen stores, recovered legs, and a sharp nervous system on race day. Every easy day now directly feeds race performance. Trust the plan: easy Thursday → modest long run Saturday → build confidence through consistency, not heroics.
